output.summary: KEP-5996 proposes a kubelet configuration field, DefaultPodSysctls, that applies default sysctls to all Pods, including static Pods. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: The sources do not give a full problem statement; reviewers asked for a concrete example of a sysctl an administrator would need to adjust across all Pods. Reviewers also asked that the KEP exclude per-namespace filtering and that unknown sysctls fail validation, so that typos are caught early. Kubelet validation was aligned with the container runtime, which ignores unnamespaced sysctls.

alternatives.why_not: Reviewer sergeykanzhelev said failing fast helps detect configuration issues, and asked for at least a log message rather than silent ignoring.

alternatives.option: Check sysctl existence in the kubelet against kernel files
alternatives.why_not: Commenter veraqin said this check might be expensive, and that value type and range can only be validated by the Linux kernel.
veraqin said DefaultPodSysctls is unrelated to AllowedUnsafeSysctls, which controls what sysctls user workloads may set.

evidence.quote: add non-goal to not include any additional filtering on which Pods those default will apply to. For e.g. we do not want to have per-Pod-namespace sets of sysctls
specify that static pods are also in-scope. Mentioning them explicitly helps to not forget to add tests for them
Yes, container runtime only does namespace validation, and thus Kubelet will also add the same validation.
This is not supported on Windows, should be denied in validation step if set on Windows
`DefaultPodSysctls` is unrelated to `AllowedUnsafeSysctls`. `AllowedUnsafeSysctls` is used for admins to decide what sysctls can be set inside user workloads.
